title: The universal finite-part groupoid over a separated etale scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be an $S$-groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]; this means that the displayed maps are $S$-maps and satisfy the groupoid laws on every test $S$-scheme. Suppose $s,t:R\to U$ are separated (closed-immersion diagonals [def-weil-closed-immersion]), flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, let $F(T)$ be the set of pairs $(a,Z)$ where $a:T\to U$ and $Z\subseteq R\times_{s,U,a}T$ is an open subscheme, finite over $T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], containing the section $(e\circ a,1_T)$. Pullback defines $F$ on test schemes. There is an $S$-scheme $M$ with a natural bijection $\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,M)\simeq F(T)$ for every $T$, under which $g:M\to U$ sends $(a,Z)$ to $a$; $g$ is separated and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. There is a universal open and closed subscheme $Q\subseteq R\times_{s,U,g}M$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product], whose pullback at $(a,Z)$ is $Z$. A $T$-point of $Q$ is a triple $(a,Z,z)$ with $z:T\to R$, $s\circ z=a$, and $(z,1_T)$ factoring through $Z$. These schemes carry a groupoid $(M,Q)$ over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] with source $(a,Z,z)\mapsto(a,Z)$ and target $(a,Z,z)\mapsto(t\circ z,Z\circ z^{-1})$. Here $Z\circ z^{-1}$ is the image of $Z$ under the translation isomorphism $R\times_{s,U,a}T\to R\times_{s,U,tz}T$, $r\mapsto c(r,i(z))$. The unit is $(a,Z,e(a))$, inverse sends $(a,Z,z)$ to $(tz,Z\circ z^{-1},i(z))$, and composition sends composable triples with arrows $z_1,z_2$ to the triple with source object $(a_2,Z_2)$ and arrow $c(z_1,z_2)$. Both projections $Q\to M$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The map $Q\to R$, $(a,Z,z)\mapsto z$, together with $g$, is a morphism of groupoids. The induced map $j:Q\to R_M:=M\times_{g,U,s}R\times_{t,U,g}M$, sending a triple to its arrow and its source and target objects, is an open immersion and a morphism of groupoids identical on objects. No affineness, local quasi-finiteness or pointed stabilizer hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04RU (lemma-finite-part-groupoid), including the preceding section-finite-part-groupoid construction; Tag 04RI (lemma-finite-separated-flat-locally-finite-presentation) and Tag 04RR (lemma-finite-plus-section) give scheme representability and separated etaleness. proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-section-marked-finite-parts-scheme] to $f=s:R\to U$ and $\sigma=e$. The groupoid unit law gives $se=1_U$, and all three morphism hypotheses are assumptions of the item. Its functor is exactly $F$, so it supplies the representing scheme $M$, the separated etale forgetful map $g$, and the universal open and closed $Q\subseteq R\times_{s,U,g}M$, finite over $M$ and containing the unit. The universal pair pulls back to the given pair by the stated natural representing bijection. The residue-field-point assertion of the cited lemma is not needed.

A finitely presented algebra has finitely many algebra generators, so the local affine definition of local finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] implies local finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; thus $s,t$ satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-universal-finite-parts-groupoid]. Apply that node to the representing $M$, the map $g$, and the universal $Q$ from step 1. It gives the claimed triple description, all five structure maps, their groupoid identities, the morphism $(M,Q)\to(U,R)$, and finiteness of both projections. In particular the translated family is the image under $r\mapsto c(r,i(z))$ with inverse $r\mapsto c(r,z)$. The hypothesis of this citation is representability already obtained in step 1; no finiteness of the entire source fibre is assumed.

proof.text: Put $P=R\times_{s,U,g}M$ and let $q:Q\to R$ be the arrow map. The projection $P\to R$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], since it is the base change of $g$. The inclusion $Q\hookrightarrow P$ is etale, and hence $q$ is etale, by clauses (1),(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. For the commutative squares $sq=gs_Q$ and $tq=gt_Q$, apply [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] with the two etale vertical maps $q,g$, first for flatness and then for local finite presentation. Since $s,t$ have these properties, so do $s_Q,t_Q$. They are finite by step 2, and therefore finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. This uses only etale base change and the cited source-and-target property, with no quasi-compactness assumption on $R$ or $U$.

source.place: Tag 04RU, universal open source projection; scheme-property argument using Descent Tags 04R1 (lemma-local-source-target-characterize), 04R3 (remark-list-local-source-target)

proof.text: The restriction $R_M=M\times_{g,U,s}R\times_{t,U,g}M$ has the groupoid operations obtained by retaining the two endpoints and using those of $R$; their identities follow componentwise. The morphism from step 2 defines $j:Q\to R_M$ by its source, arrow and target. Comparing these three projections shows that $j$ respects every operation and is identical on objects. Forgetting the target gives $p:R_M\to P$, the base change of the separated etale map $g$ along $P\to U$, $(r,m)\mapsto t(r)$. It is separated etale by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Its pullback $E=Q\times_P R_M\to Q$ has both properties by the same nodes. Since $pj$ is the inclusion $Q\hookrightarrow P$, $j$ gives a section $k:Q\to E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion], $k$ is an open immersion. Also $E\to R_M$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Their composite is $j$. A composite of two isomorphisms onto open subschemes is again such an isomorphism, so [def-weil-open-immersion] gives the required open immersion.

Step 1: lem-sfb-section-marked-finite-parts-scheme with f=s, σ=e (se=1); its functor is exactly F and it gives M, separated étale g and the clopen finite Q; the quasi-finite residue clause is correctly unused. Step 3: q:Q→R is étale (open immersion, then base change of g, then composition clauses (1) and (2)). The squares s∘q=g∘s_Q and t∘q=g∘t_Q fit the 'P(f)⇒P(h)' clause of lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties for flatness and lfp, so s_Q and t_Q are finite locally free. Step 4: R_M→P is the base change of g, so it is separated and étale. Since p∘j is the inclusion Q↪P, (1,j) is a section of E=Q×_P R_M→Q, hence an open immersion by the etale-section-clopen node; E→R_M is a base change of an open immersion, so the composite j is an open immersion.
